     1	// reference/src/semantics/controls.k — MPY-CONTROLS
     2	
     3	module MPY-CONTROLS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	  imports MPY-TUPLE
     6	  imports MPY-ITER
     7	
     8	  // ==== Assign / AugAssign (write the current scope; RHS evaluated by strictness) ==
     9	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    10	       <env> L:Int </env>
    11	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    12	  rule <k> Assign(Name(X:String), V:Val) => #cellW({M[X]}:>Val, V) ... </k>
    13	       <env> L:Int </env>
    14	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    15	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    16	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    17	        andBool X in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[X]}:>Val)
    18	       [priority(40)]
    19	
    20	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => .K ... </k>
    21	       <env> L:Int </env>
    22	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ X <- applyBin(OP, {M[X]}:>Val, V) ], _) ... </scopes>
    23	       requires X in_keys(M)
    24	  // `lst += [..]` where lst is a heap ref: the generic rule leaves applyBin(OP, ref, V) — but the
    25	  // ref-deref preemption is BinOp-level (operators.k), so applyBin never derefs and it sticks. Route
    26	  // the ref case through BinOp so the deref + list-concat + #alloc path fires (result is a fresh ref).
    27	  rule <k> AugAssign(Name(X:String), OP:String, V:Val) => Assign(Name(X), BinOp(OP, Name(X), V)) ... </k>
    28	       <env> L:Int </env>
    29	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    30	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool isRefV({M[X]}:>Val)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // ==== import trivia: `from math import floor, ceil` binds the supported
    34	  // names as builtins in the current scope; every other import is a no-op
    35	  rule <k> ImportFrom("math", NS:ParamNames) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> ImportFrom(_:String, _:ParamNames) => .K ... </k> [owise]
    37	  syntax KItem ::= #bindImports(ParamNames)
    38	  rule <k> #bindImports(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    39	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    40	       <env> L:Int </env>
    41	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ N <- builtinV(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    42	       requires N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil"
    43	  rule <k> #bindImports((N:String, NS:ParamNames)) => #bindImports(NS) ... </k>
    44	       requires notBool (N ==String "floor" orBool N ==String "ceil")
    45	
    46	  // ==== Expr statement: evaluate for effect, discard the value ===============
    47	  // (bare calls — mutator methods, docstrings; the WP0 statement-trivia rung)
    48	  rule <k> Expr(_:Val) => .K ... </k>
    49	
    50	  // ==== If (condition evaluated by strictness) ==============================
    51	  syntax KItem ::= #branch(Bool, Stmts, Stmts)
    52	  rule <k> If(C:Val, T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => #branch(truthy(C), T, E) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #branch(true,  T:Stmts, _:Stmts) => T ... </k>
    54	  rule <k> #branch(false, _:Stmts, E:Stmts) => E ... </k>
    55	
    56	  // ==== IfExp: ternary T if C else E ========================================
    57	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, T:Expr, _:Expr) => T ... </k>
    58	       requires truthy(V)
    59	  rule <k> IfExp(V:Val, _:Expr, E:Expr) => E ... </k>
    60	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    61	
    62	  // ==== For: one loop, in-cell continuation, over #iterNext =================
    63	  // (the iterable is evaluated once, by strictness; the protocol stays rewrites —
    64	  // circularities anchor on #loop and narrowing substitutes the structure)
    65	  syntax KItem ::= #loop(Val, Expr, Stmts) | #loopStep(Expr, Stmts)
    66	                 | #while(Expr, Stmts) | #whileCond(Expr, Stmts)
    67	                 | #loopLbl(K) | "#cont" | "#brk"
    68	
    69	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, OBJ:Val, B:Stmts) => #loop(OBJ, T, B) ... </k>
    70	
    71	  rule <k> #loop(IT:Iterable, T:Expr, B:Stmts) => #iterNext(IT) ~> #loopStep(T, B) ... </k>
    72	  rule <k> #iterDone ~> #loopStep(_:Expr, _:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    73	  rule <k> #iterYield(V:Val, REST:Iterable) ~> #loopStep(T:Expr, B:Stmts)
    74	        => #bindTgt(T, V) ~> B ~> #loopLbl(#loop(REST, T, B)) ... </k>
    75	
    76	  // ==== While ==============================================================
    77	  rule <k> While(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => #while(C, B) ... </k>
    78	  rule <k> #while(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => C ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
    79	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => B ~> #loopLbl(#while(C, B)) ... </k>
    80	       requires truthy(V)
    81	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #whileCond(_C:Expr, _B:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    82	       requires notBool truthy(V)
    83	
    84	  // ==== loop control (break / continue) =====================================
    85	  rule <k> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    86	  rule <k> Continue => #cont ... </k>
    87	  rule <k> Break => #brk ... </k>
    88	  rule <k> #cont ~> #loopLbl(NEXT:K) => NEXT ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #cont ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    90	  rule <k> #brk ~> #loopLbl(_:K) => .K ... </k>
    91	  rule <k> #brk ~> (_:KItem => .K) ... </k> [owise]
    92	
    93	  // ==== heap-object deref at the truthiness/iteration consumers ==============
    94	  // (priority(40) preempts the generic Val rules so truthy/#loop never see a ref)
    95	  rule <k> If(ref(H:Int), T:Stmts, E:Stmts) => If(V, T, E) ... </k>
    96	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    97	       [priority(40)]
    98	  rule <k> IfExp(ref(H:Int), T:Expr, E:Expr) => IfExp(V, T, E) ... </k>
    99	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   100	       [priority(40)]
   101	  rule <k> ref(H:Int) ~> #whileCond(C:Expr, B:Stmts) => V ~> #whileCond(C, B) ... </k>
   102	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   103	       [priority(40)]
   104	  // For derefs its iterable ONCE at loop start (iteration is over the snapshot;
   105	  // mutating the iterated list inside its own loop is outside the subset)
   106	  rule <k> For(T:Expr, ref(H:Int), B:Stmts) => For(T, V, B) ... </k>
   107	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
   108	       [priority(40)]

### /reference/reference-semantics/semantics/operators.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/operators.k — MPY-OPERATORS
     2	// The operator DISPATCH layer: operands evaluate by strictness (heat/cool over KResult=Val),
     3	// the cooled node hands to applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp (declared in core.k; each domain file
     4	// owns its cases — bool.k, int.k, float.k, str.k, list.k, tuple.k, set.k, dict.k).
     5	
     6	module MPY-OPERATORS
     7	  imports MPY-CORE
     8	  imports MPY-ITER
     9	
    10	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, V:Val) => applyUn(OP, V) ... </k>
    11	
    12	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, R:Val) => applyBin(OP, L, R) ... </k>
    13	
    14	  // Compare's right operand sits under the CmpOp wrapper — contexts instead of attributes
    15	  context Compare(HOLE, _)
    16	  context Compare(_:Val, CmpOp(_, HOLE))
    17	  rule <k> Compare(LV:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, RV:Val)) => applyCmp(OP, LV, RV) ... </k> [owise]
    18	
    19	  rule applyCmp("is",     V:Val, noneV) => V ==K noneV
    20	  rule applyCmp("is not", V:Val, noneV) => notBool (V ==K noneV)
    21	
    22	  // ==== operand deref: heap objects combine/compare by STRUCTURE ============
    23	  // (Python: list == is structural; identity only via `is`.) priority(40)
    24	  // preempts the generic dispatch so applyUn/applyBin/applyCmp never see a ref.
    25	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int), R:Expr) => BinOp(OP, V, R) ... </k>
    26	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    27	       [priority(40)]
    28	  rule <k> BinOp(OP:String, L:Val, ref(H:Int)) => BinOp(OP, L, V) ... </k>
    29	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    30	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    31	       [priority(40)]
    32	
    33	  // the left operand of `in`/`not in` is an ELEMENT (compares by ==K) — never deref'd
    34	  rule <k> Compare(ref(H:Int), CmpOp(OP:String, R:Expr)) => Compare(V, CmpOp(OP, R)) ... </k>
    35	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    36	       requires OP =/=String "in" andBool OP =/=String "not in"
    37	       [priority(40)]
    38	  rule <k> Compare(L:Val, CmpOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int))) => Compare(L, CmpOp(OP, V)) ... </k>
    39	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    40	       requires notBool isRefV(L)
    41	        orBool OP ==String "in" orBool OP ==String "not in"
    42	       [priority(40)]
    43	
    44	  rule <k> UnaryOp(OP:String, ref(H:Int)) => UnaryOp(OP, V) ... </k>
    45	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	endmodule

    10	  // Bool participates in int arithmetic (x += (a == b))
    11	  rule applyBin("+",  I:Int, B:Bool) => I +Int #if B #then 1 #else 0 #fi

    13	  rule applyBin("-",  I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 -Int I2

    16	  rule applyBin("//", I1:Int, I2:Int) => (I1 -Int pyMod(I1, I2)) /Int I2
    17	  rule applyBin("**", I1:Int, I2:Int) => I1 ^Int I2 requires I2 >=Int 0
    18	
    19	  syntax Int ::= pyMod(Int, Int) [function]
    20	  rule pyMod(I1:Int, I2:Int) => ((I1 %Int I2) +Int I2) %Int I2

    24	  rule applyCmp(">",  I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >Int  I2
    25	  rule applyCmp(">=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 >=Int I2
    26	  rule applyCmp("==", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 ==Int I2
    27	  rule applyCmp("!=", I1:Int, I2:Int)   => I1 =/=Int I2

   100	  syntax Bool ::= isKwV(Val) [function, total]
   101	  rule isKwV(kwV(_:String, _:Val)) => true
   102	  rule isKwV(_:Val)                => false [owise]
   103	
   104	  // the frame marker carries the CONCRETE cellvar list, so cell-write dispatch
   105	  // decides by pnMember even over an abstract frame rest (no prover branching)
   106	  syntax Val ::= cellsMark(ParamNames)
   107	  syntax ParamNames ::= cellsOf(Val) [function]
   108	  rule cellsOf(cellsMark(CVS:ParamNames)) => CVS
   109	  syntax Bool ::= pnMember(String, ParamNames) [function, total]
   110	  rule pnMember(_:String, .ParamNames) => false
   111	  rule pnMember(X:String, (P:String, R:ParamNames)) => X ==String P orBool pnMember(X, R)
   112	
   113	  syntax KItem ::= #cellW(Val, Val)
   114	  rule <k> #cellW(cellRef(H:Int), V:Val) => .K ... </k>
   115	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(_:Val => V) ... </heap>
   116	
   117	  syntax KItem ::= #alloc(Val)
   118	  rule <k> #alloc(V:Val) => ref(N) ... </k>
   119	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> V) H </heap>
   120	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
   121	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
   122	
   123	  // ==== module load + statement sequencing ==================================
   124	  syntax KItem ::= #loadAll(Module)
   125	  rule <k> #loadAll(Module(SS:Stmts)) => SS ... </k>
   126	  rule <k> (S:Stmt SS:Stmts):Stmts => S ~> SS ... </k>
   127	  rule <k> .Stmts => .K ... </k>
   128	
   129	  // ==== Name lookup (walk the scope chain; builtins live in the -1 scope) ====
   130	  syntax KItem ::= #look(String, Int)
   131	  rule <k> Name(X:String) => #look(X, L) ... </k> <env> L:Int </env>
   132	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => {M[X]}:>Val ... </k>
   133	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   134	       requires X in_keys(M)
   135	  // a SYNTACTICALLY cell-bound name reads through the heap cell AT THE
   136	  // LOOKUP (higher priority beats the plain return above on concrete cell
   137	  // bindings; abstract claim values take the plain rule unchanged) — this
   138	  // covers cross-frame cell reads (a comprehension closure reading the
   139	  // enclosing function's cellvar) without a narrowing-prone k-top redex
   140	  // guarded on the FOUND frame's DECLARED cellvars (pnMember over the
   141	  // cellsMark): decidable for every concrete frame pin — plain frames and
   142	  // non-cell names prune outright, so an abstract looked-up value never
   143	  // drags a narrowing cellV heap match along (probed on 5-intersperse and
   144	  // Q4's abstract `numbers` in the annotated frame)
   145	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => V ... </k>
   146	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _:Parent) ... </scopes>
   147	       <heap> ... H |-> cellV(V:Val) ... </heap>
   148	       requires X in_keys(M) andBool "$cells" in_keys(M)
   149	        andBool pnMember(X, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
   150	        andBool {M[X]}:>Val ==K cellRef(H)
   151	       [priority(40)]
   152	  rule <k> #look(X:String, L:Int) => #look(X, P) ... </k>
   153	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, parent(P:Int)) ... </scopes>
   154	       requires notBool (X in_keys(M))
   155	
   156	  // the ONE predefined builtins scope (the -1 frame; claims write `-1 |-> builtinsScope`)
   157	  syntax Scope ::= "builtinsScope" [function, total]
   158	  rule builtinsScope
   159	    => scope(.Map [ "len"    <- builtinV("len")    ]
   160	                  [ "set"    <- builtinV("set")    ]
   161	                  [ "sum"    <- builtinV("sum")    ]
   162	                  [ "abs"    <- builtinV("abs")    ]
   163	                  [ "min"    <- builtinV("min")    ]
   164	                  [ "max"    <- builtinV("max")    ]
   165	                  [ "ord"    <- builtinV("ord")    ]
   166	                  [ "chr"    <- builtinV("chr")    ]
   167	                  [ "range"  <- builtinV("range")  ]
   168	                  [ "all"    <- builtinV("all")    ]
   169	                  [ "any"    <- builtinV("any")    ]
   170	                  [ "zip"    <- builtinV("zip")    ]
   171	                  [ "isinstance" <- builtinV("isinstance") ]
   172	                  [ "sorted" <- builtinV("sorted") ]
   173	                  [ "list"   <- builtinV("list")   ]
   174	                  [ "round"  <- builtinV("round")  ]
   175	                  [ "bin"    <- builtinV("bin")    ]
   176	                  [ "enumerate" <- builtinV("enumerate") ]
   177	                  [ "map"    <- builtinV("map")    ]
   178	                  [ "eval"   <- builtinV("eval")   ]
   179	                  [ "int"    <- typeV("int")       ]
   180	                  [ "str"    <- typeV("str")       ]
   181	                  [ "float"  <- typeV("float")     ], root)
   182	
   183	  // ==== argument/element evaluation: ONE left-to-right loop, tagged by destination ==
   184	  // (list/tuple literals and calls all use it; modules extend ApplyK with their tags)
   185	  syntax ApplyK ::= toCall(Val)
   186	  syntax KItem  ::= #evalArgs(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   187	                  | #evalArgCont(Exprs, Vals, ApplyK)
   188	                  | #applyK(ApplyK, Vals)
   189	  rule <k> #evalArgs((A:Expr, REST:Exprs), ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => A ~> #evalArgCont(REST, ACC, K) ... </k>
   190	  rule <k> V:Val ~> #evalArgCont(REST:Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #evalArgs(REST, appendVal(ACC, V), K) ... </k>
   191	  rule <k> #evalArgs(.Exprs, ACC:Vals, K:ApplyK) => #applyK(K, ACC) ... </k>
   192	
   193	  // ==== Int / Bool / None literals ==========================================
   194	  rule <k> Int(I:Int)   => I ... </k>
   195	  rule <k> Bool(B:Bool) => B ... </k>
   196	  rule <k> NoneVal      => noneV ... </k>
   197	
   198	  // ==== truthy (If, Assert, BoolOp, IfExp, not, While) ======================
   199	  syntax Bool ::= truthy(Val) [function]
   200	  rule truthy(B:Bool)          => B
   201	  rule truthy(noneV)           => false
   202	  rule truthy(I:Int)           => I =/=Int 0
   203	  rule truthy(str(S:IntSeq))   => notBool (S ==K .IntSeq)
   204	  rule truthy(list(V:ValSeq))  => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   205	  rule truthy(tuple(V:ValSeq)) => notBool (V ==K .ValSeq)
   206	
   207	  // ==== extensible operator dispatch (cases added by the construct modules) ==
   208	  syntax Val  ::= applyUn(String, Val) [function]
   209	  syntax Val  ::= applyBin(String, Val, Val) [function]
   210	  syntax Bool ::= applyCmp(String, Val, Val) [function]
   211	
   212	  // ==== shared list helpers =================================================
   213	  syntax Vals ::= appendVal(Vals, Val) [function, total]
   214	  rule appendVal(.Vals, V:Val)              => V , .Vals
   215	  rule appendVal((V0:Val, VS:Vals), V:Val)  => V0 , appendVal(VS, V)
   216	
   217	  syntax ValSeq ::= vals2valSeq(Vals) [function, total]
   218	  rule vals2valSeq(.Vals)            => .ValSeq
   219	  rule vals2valSeq((V:Val, VS:Vals)) => vCons(V, vals2valSeq(VS))
   220	
   221	  // ==== shared sequence length (len / summaries across many modules) ========
   222	  // (positional access valSeqAt/intSeqAt + normIdx live in subscript.k)
   223	  syntax Int ::= vsLen(ValSeq) [function, total]
   224	  rule vsLen(.ValSeq)                => 0
   225	  rule vsLen(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq)) => 1 +Int vsLen(S)

   227	  syntax Int ::= isLen(IntSeq) [function, total]

   229	  rule isLen(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq)) => 1 +Int isLen(S)
   230	
   231	  // in-bounds positional write (list subscript-assign); OOB leaves the seq unchanged
   232	  // (valid programs write in-bounds — mirrors valSeqAt's total-but-underspecified stance)
   233	  syntax ValSeq ::= setVSAt(ValSeq, Int, Val) [function, total]

### /reference/reference-semantics/semantics/functions.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/functions.k — MPY-FUNCTIONS
     2	
     3	module MPY-FUNCTIONS
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // call routing + callee/arg evaluation (#callee/#args/#argCont) live in call.k;
     7	  // this module owns the frame lifecycle (bind params, return, pop).
     8	  syntax KItem ::= frame(continuation: K, callerEnv: Int, savedLoc: Int)
     9	                 | #bindP(ParamNames, Vals)
    10	                 | "#pop"
    11	                 | "#endcall"
    12	
    13	  // ==== def / anonymous closure =============================================
    14	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts) => .K ... </k>
    15	       <env> L:Int </env>
    16	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ], _) ... </scopes>
    17	
    18	  syntax Expr ::= closureExpr(ParamNames, Stmts)
    19	  rule <k> closureExpr(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts) => closureVal(PNS, BODY, L) ... </k>
    20	       <env> L:Int </env>
    21	
    22	  // ==== annotated def/lambda (closure cells; spec 2.3) ======================
    23	  // closureValC(params, cellvars, body, captured-cells). No frame anchor: all
    24	  // enclosing-local reads are freevars (symtable-complete) and go through the
    25	  // captured cells; everything else is global/builtin, so the callee frame's
    26	  // parent is the module scope (0) — sound after the defining frame dies.
    27	  syntax Val ::= closureValC(ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    28	
    29	  // capture: resolve each freevar to the enclosing frame's cellRef, then bind
    30	  // (FuncDef) or yield (Lambda) the closure value.
    31	  syntax KItem ::= #mkClosure(String, ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    32	                 | #mkLambda(ParamNames, ParamNames, ParamNames, Stmts, Map)
    33	  rule <k> FuncDef(F:String, Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    34	                   FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts)
    35	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVS, BODY, .Map) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    37	                      (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    38	        => #mkClosure(F, PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    39	       <env> L:Int </env>
    40	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    41	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    42	  rule <k> #mkClosure(F:String, PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    43	                      .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map) => .K ... </k>
    44	       <env> L:Int </env>
    45	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ F <- closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ], _) ... </scopes>
    46	
    47	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    48	        => closureVal(PNS, Return(E) .Stmts, L) ... </k>
    49	       <env> L:Int </env>
    50	  rule <k> Lambda(Params(PNS:ParamNames), CellVars(CVS:ParamNames),
    51	                  FreeVars(FVS:ParamNames), E:Expr)
    52	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVS, Return(E) .Stmts, .Map) ... </k>
    53	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames,
    54	                     (FV:String, FVR:ParamNames), BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    55	        => #mkLambda(PNS, CVS, FVR, BODY, CM [ FV <- {M[FV]}:>Val ]) ... </k>
    56	       <env> L:Int </env>
    57	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    58	       requires FV in_keys(M)
    59	  rule <k> #mkLambda(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, .ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)
    60	        => closureValC(PNS, CVS, BODY, CM) ... </k>
    61	
    62	  // ==== bind params ========================================================
    63	  rule <k> #bindP(.ParamNames, .Vals) => .K ... </k>
    64	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals)) => #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    65	       <env> L:Int </env>
    66	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ P <- V ], _) ... </scopes>
    67	  // a param that is a cellvar was pre-bound to its cell at frame entry
    68	  rule <k> #bindP((P:String, PS:ParamNames), (V:Val, VS:Vals))
    69	        => #cellW({M[P]}:>Val, V) ~> #bindP(PS, VS) ... </k>
    70	       <env> L:Int </env>
    71	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map, _) ... </scopes>
    72	       requires "$cells" in_keys(M)
    73	        andBool pnMember(P, cellsOf({M["$cells"]}:>Val))
    74	        andBool P in_keys(M) andBool isCellRef({M[P]}:>Val)
    75	       [priority(40)]
    76	
    77	  // ==== return / pop the frame (the returned expr evaluates by strictness) ==
    78	  rule <k> Return(V:Val) ~> _ => #pop </k>
    79	       <ret> noRet => retV(V) </ret>
    80	  rule <k> #endcall => #pop ... </k>
    81	       <ret> noRet => retV(noneV) </ret>
    82	  // pop: restore env, DEALLOCATE the callee frame, and wind scopeLoc back (LIFO allocation
    83	  // makes the saved loc the callee frame's own loc). Sound because no closureVal outlives its
    84	  // defining frame (frontend subset: no returned/stored closures; module defs live in loc 0).
    85	  rule <k> #pop => V ~> CONT </k>
    86	       <ret>   retV(V) => noRet </ret>
    87	       <stack> ListItem(frame(CONT:K, CALLERL:Int, SAVEDL:Int)) => .List ... </stack>
    88	       <env>   L:Int => CALLERL </env>
    89	       <scopes> SC:Map => SC [ L <- undef ] </scopes>
    90	       <scopeLoc> _ => SAVEDL </scopeLoc>
    91	endmodule

### /reference/reference-semantics/semantics/call.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/call.k — MPY-CALL
     2	// ONE call route for every callable: evaluate the callee to a VALUE (name lookup reaches
     3	// builtins at the root; a cooled Attribute is a bound method), evaluate the args (the shared
     4	// #evalArgs loop in core.k), then dispatch on the callee value:
     5	//   closureVal    -> bind params, push a frame (user function)
     6	//   boundMethodV  -> applyMethod
     7	//   builtinV      -> the #iterNext folds (sum/all/any/max/min) or applyBuiltin
     8	//   typeV         -> callable type objects: int(...) / str(...)
     9	
    10	module MPY-CALL
    11	  imports MPY-METHODS
    12	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    13	  imports MPY-FUNCTIONS
    14	
    15	  // a cooled attribute is a bound method value
    16	  rule <k> Attribute(V:Val, M:String) => boundMethodV(V, M) ... </k>
    17	
    18	  // evaluate callee, then args ([owise]: problem-local Call interceptions beat this)
    19	  syntax KItem ::= #callee(Exprs)
    20	  rule <k> Call(Fe:Expr, ARGS:Exprs) => Fe ~> #callee(ARGS) ... </k> [owise]
    21	  rule <k> CV:Val ~> #callee(ARGS:Exprs) => #evalArgs(ARGS, .Vals, toCall(CV)) ... </k>
    22	
    23	  // ==== dispatch on the callee value ========================================
    24	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyMethod(OBJ, M, ACC) ... </k>
    25	
    26	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sum")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #sumAcc(OBJ, 0) ... </k>
    27	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("all")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #allAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("any")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #anyAcc(OBJ)    ... </k>
    29	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("max")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #maxAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    30	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("min")), (OBJ:Iterable, .Vals)) => #minAcc0(OBJ)   ... </k>
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(BN, ACC) ... </k> [owise]
    32	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)),     ACC:Vals) => applyBuiltin(T, ACC)  ... </k>
    33	
    34	  // ==== heap-object arguments/receivers =====================================
    35	  // Builtins and type calls READ structure — deref the first two arg positions
    36	  // (covers len/sum/all/any/max/min/sorted/list/set + zip's pair). Mutating list
    37	  // methods take the ref itself; every other method receiver is deref'd.
    38	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    39	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    40	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    41	       [priority(40)]
    42	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN:String)), (A:Val, ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    43	        => #applyK(toCall(builtinV(BN)), (A, V, REST)) ... </k>
    44	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    45	       requires notBool isRefV(A)
    46	       [priority(40)]
    47	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(typeV(T:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    48	        => #applyK(toCall(typeV(T)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    49	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    50	       [priority(40)]
    51	
    52	  syntax Bool ::= isMutMethod(String) [function, total]
    53	  rule isMutMethod(M:String)
    54	    => M ==String "append" orBool M ==String "sort" orBool M ==String "extend"
    55	       orBool M ==String "insert" orBool M ==String "pop" orBool M ==String "remove"
    56	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(ref(H:Int), M:String)), ACC:Vals)
    57	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(V, M)), ACC) ... </k>
    58	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    59	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M)
    60	       [priority(40)]
    61	  // non-mutating methods READ their heap-object arguments too (join's list);
    62	  // mutators keep refs (append of a list into a list-of-lists stays aliased)
    63	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ:Val, M:String)), (ref(H:Int), REST:Vals))
    64	        => #applyK(toCall(boundMethodV(OBJ, M)), (V, REST)) ... </k>
    65	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    66	       requires notBool isMutMethod(M) andBool notBool isRefV(OBJ)
    67	       [priority(40)]
    68	
    69	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureVal(PNS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, DEFL:Int)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    70	        => #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    71	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    72	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(.Map, parent(DEFL)) ] </scopes>
    73	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    74	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    75	
    76	  // annotated closure: the frame starts with the captured freevar cells, its
    77	  // parent is the module scope (all enclosing-local reads go through cells),
    78	  // and the cellvars' fresh cells allocate before params bind (a cellvar param
    79	  // then writes through its cell in #bindP).
    80	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(closureValC(PNS:ParamNames, CVS:ParamNames, BODY:Stmts, CM:Map)), ACC:Vals) ~> CONT
    81	        => #allocCells(CVS) ~> #bindP(PNS, ACC) ~> BODY ~> #endcall </k>
    82	       <env>     CALLERL:Int => NEWL </env>
    83	       <scopes>   STORE:Map => STORE [ NEWL <- scope(CM [ "$cells" <- cellsMark(CVS) ], parent(0)) ] </scopes>
    84	       <scopeLoc> NEWL:Int => NEWL +Int 1 </scopeLoc>
    85	       <stack>   .List => ListItem(frame(CONT, CALLERL, NEWL)) ... </stack>
    86	
    87	  syntax KItem ::= #allocCells(ParamNames)
    88	  rule <k> #allocCells(.ParamNames) => .K ... </k>
    89	  rule <k> #allocCells((CV:String, R:ParamNames)) => #allocCells(R) ... </k>
    90	       <env> L:Int </env>
    91	       <scopes> ... L |-> scope(M:Map => M [ CV <- cellRef(N) ], _) ... </scopes>
    92	       <heap>    H:Map => (N |-> cellV(noneV)) H </heap>
    93	       <heapLoc> N:Int => N +Int 1 </heapLoc>
    94	       requires notBool N in_keys(H)
    95	endmodule

### /reference/reference-semantics/semantics/sort.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/sort.k — MPY-SORT
     2	// Trusted sorted(): sorted(list) as an opaque ascending permutation `sortVS` — opaque symbolic
     3	// for kprove (a trusted primitive, correctness/ordering proved in Lean / notes/sort-probe),
     4	// and a concrete insertion sort for krun. Wrappers verify the logic AROUND the sort (index /
     5	// slice / filter / dedup); indexing an opaque sortVS(VS) carries through as an opaque term, so
     6	// no ordering lemma is needed in K — the trust (sortVS = real sorted) is discharged by each
     7	// problem's differential test. Only int lists (compared by projectIntTotal); keyed / string
     8	// sorts are separate. Fires only via the "sorted" builtin, so inert for non-sorting programs.
     9	
    10	module MPY-SORT
    11	  imports MPY-BUILTINS
    12	  imports MPY-SUBSCRIPT
    13	
    14	  // sortVS(VS): the ascending sort of the Val list VS. Opaque for symbolic VS (no-evaluators);
    15	  // concrete insertion sort for krun.
    16	  // Concrete sort matches Int-sorted elements directly (an int Val IS an Int); projectIntTotal
    17	  // (lemmas-only) is not available in the semantics. Int and str lists.
    18	  syntax ValSeq ::= sortVS(ValSeq) [function, total, symbol(sortVS), no-evaluators]
    19	  syntax ValSeq ::= insVS(Int, ValSeq) [function]
    20	  rule sortVS(.ValSeq)                => .ValSeq          [concrete]
    21	  rule sortVS(vCons(X:Int, R:ValSeq)) => insVS(X, sortVS(R)) [concrete]
    22	  rule insVS(X:Int, .ValSeq)                => vCons(X, .ValSeq) [concrete]
    23	  rule insVS(X:Int, vCons(Y:Int, R:ValSeq)) => vCons(X, vCons(Y, R)) requires X <=Int Y [concrete]

### /reference/reference-semantics/semantics/subscript.k
     1	// reference/src/semantics/subscript.k — MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     2	
     3	module MPY-SUBSCRIPT
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // ==== positional access + negative-index normalization (used only here) ===
     7	  // valSeqAt is [total]: in-bounds vCons access reduces as usual; on an OPAQUE sequence (e.g.
     8	  // a trusted sort's sortVS(VS)) or OOB it stays an abstract total value — so indexing the
     9	  // opaque sorted list is DEFINED (no undischarged #Ceil), matching the old semantics' total
    10	  // atK. K trusts the [total] annotation; valid programs index in-bounds.
    11	  syntax Val ::= valSeqAt(ValSeq, Int) [function, total]
    12	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(V:Val, _:ValSeq), 0)     => V
    13	  rule valSeqAt(vCons(_:Val, S:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    14	       requires I >Int 0
    15	
    16	  syntax Int ::= intSeqAt(IntSeq, Int) [function]
    17	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(C:Int, _:IntSeq), 0)     => C
    18	  rule intSeqAt(iCons(_:Int, S:IntSeq), I:Int) => intSeqAt(S, I -Int 1)
    19	       requires I >Int 0
    20	
    21	  syntax Int ::= normIdx(Int, Int) [function, total]
    22	  rule normIdx(I:Int, LEN:Int) => I +Int LEN requires I  <Int 0
    23	  rule normIdx(I:Int, _:Int)   => I          requires I >=Int 0
    24	
    25	  // ==== Subscript: indexing obj[i] (list / tuple / str) =====================
    26	  // contexts (not strict attrs): the Index slot's Slice alternative must never heat
    27	  context Subscript(HOLE, _)
    28	  context Subscript(_:Val, HOLE:Expr)
    29	
    30	  // heap-object deref (covers both the index and slice forms via the Index slot)
    31	  rule <k> Subscript(ref(H:Int), IX:Index) => Subscript(V, IX) ... </k>
    32	       <heap> ... H |-> V:Val ... </heap>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	
    35	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, I:Int) => applyIndex(OBJ, I) ... </k>
    36	
    37	  syntax Val ::= applyIndex(Val, Int) [function]
    38	  rule applyIndex(list(VS:ValSeq),  I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    39	  rule applyIndex(tuple(VS:ValSeq), I:Int) => valSeqAt(VS, normIdx(I, vsLen(VS)))
    40	  rule applyIndex(str(IS:IntSeq),   I:Int)
    41	    => str(iCons(intSeqAt(IS, normIdx(I, isLen(IS))), .IntSeq))
    42	
    43	  // ==== Slice: obj[lo:hi:step] (list / str) — CPython slice.indices ==========
    44	  syntax KItem ::= #evalB(Bound) | "#toSome"
    45	                 | #slLo(Val, Bound, Bound)
    46	                 | #slHi(Val, OptInt, Bound)
    47	                 | #slStep(Val, OptInt, OptInt)
    48	
    49	  syntax OptInt ::= "noB" | someB(Int)
    50	  rule <k> #evalB(NoBound)  => noB ... </k>
    51	  rule <k> #evalB(E:Expr)   => E ~> #toSome ... </k>
    52	  rule <k> I:Int ~> #toSome => someB(I) ... </k>
    53	
    54	  rule <k> Subscript(OBJ:Val, Slice(LO:Bound, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)) => #evalB(LO) ~> #slLo(OBJ, HI, ST) ... </k>
    55	  rule <k> LO:OptInt ~> #slLo(OBJ:Val, HI:Bound, ST:Bound)   => #evalB(HI) ~> #slHi(OBJ, LO, ST) ... </k>
    56	  rule <k> HI:OptInt ~> #slHi(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, ST:Bound)  => #evalB(ST) ~> #slStep(OBJ, LO, HI) ... </k>
    57	  // a list slice constructs a NEW object; a str slice stays a value
    58	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt)
    59	        => #alloc(doSlice(list(VS), LO, HI, ST)) ... </k>
    60	       [priority(45)]
    61	  rule <k> ST:OptInt ~> #slStep(OBJ:Val, LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt) => doSlice(OBJ, LO, HI, ST) ... </k>
    62	
    63	  syntax Val ::= doSlice(Val, OptInt, OptInt, OptInt) [function]
    64	  rule doSlice(list(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    65	    => list(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    66	  rule doSlice(tuple(VS:ValSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    67	    => tuple(buildVS(VS, slStart(LO, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStop(HI, ST, vsLen(VS)), slStep(ST)))
    68	  rule doSlice(str(IS:IntSeq), LO:OptInt, HI:OptInt, ST:OptInt)
    69	    => str(buildIS(IS, slStart(LO, ST, isLen(IS)), slStop(HI, ST, isLen(IS)), slStep(ST)))
    70	
    71	  // ==== slice.indices: step / start / stop / clamp ==========================
    72	  syntax Int ::= slStep(OptInt) [function, total]
    73	  rule slStep(noB)          => 1
    74	  rule slStep(someB(S:Int)) => S
    75	
    76	  syntax Int ::= slStart(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    77	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => 0
    78	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    79	  rule slStart(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN -Int 1
    80	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    81	  rule slStart(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    82	
    83	  syntax Int ::= slStop(OptInt, OptInt, Int) [function]
    84	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => LEN
    85	       requires slStep(ST) >Int 0
    86	  rule slStop(noB,          ST:OptInt, _LEN:Int) => -1
    87	       requires slStep(ST) <Int 0
    88	  rule slStop(someB(I:Int), ST:OptInt, LEN:Int)  => slAdjust(I, LEN, slStep(ST))
    89	
    90	  syntax Int ::= slAdjust(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
    91	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampLo(I +Int LEN, STEP)
    92	       requires I  <Int 0
    93	  rule slAdjust(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int) => clampHi(I, LEN, STEP)
    94	       requires I >=Int 0
    95	
    96	  syntax Int ::= clampLo(Int, Int) [function, total]
    97	  rule clampLo(J:Int, _STEP:Int) => J
    98	       requires J >=Int 0
    99	  rule clampLo(J:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then -1 #else 0 #fi
   100	       requires J <Int 0
   101	
   102	  syntax Int ::= clampHi(Int, Int, Int) [function, total]
   103	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, _STEP:Int) => I
   104	       requires I  <Int LEN
   105	  rule clampHi(I:Int, LEN:Int, STEP:Int)  => #if STEP <Int 0 #then LEN -Int 1 #else LEN #fi
   106	       requires I >=Int LEN
   107	
   108	  // ==== build the strided sub-sequence (indices in range by construction) ====
   109	  syntax ValSeq ::= buildVS(ValSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   110	  rule buildVS(VS:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   111	    => vCons(valSeqAt(VS, I), buildVS(VS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   112	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   113	  rule buildVS(_:ValSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .ValSeq
   114	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   115	
   116	  syntax IntSeq ::= buildIS(IntSeq, Int, Int, Int) [function]
   117	  rule buildIS(IS:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int)
   118	    => iCons(intSeqAt(IS, I), buildIS(IS, I +Int STEP, STOP, STEP))
   119	       requires (STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP)
   120	  rule buildIS(_:IntSeq, I:Int, STOP:Int, STEP:Int) => .IntSeq
   121	       requires notBool ((STEP >Int 0 andBool I <Int STOP) orBool (STEP <Int 0 andBool I >Int STOP))
   122	endmodule

     2	//
     3	// Minimal dict support. A dict value is `dictV(KS, VS)`: PARALLEL insertion-ordered key/value
     4	// ValSeqs (Python dict order; keys distinct; re-inserting a key updates its value in place, keeping
     5	// the original position). Concrete for krun (the ordered build + `.keys()` are the real ops); a proof
     6	// over a SYMBOLIC dict passes `dictV(KS, WS)` with a symbolic key sequence KS and reads
     7	// `d.keys() = list(KS)`, then keeps each key opaque problem-locally.
     8	//
     9	// Only the pieces needed so far: a dict VALUE (so `{}` inside a mixed list evaluates and
    10	// `isinstance(x, int)` rejects it), the `{k: v, ...}` literal, and `.keys()`. More dict ops (subscript
    11	// / `.get()` / `.values()` / dict `==`) are added as dict problems need them — kept minimal + additive.

    14	  imports MPY-CORE
    15	  imports MPY-ITER
    16	  imports MPY-METHODS
    17	  imports MPY-LIST

    19	  // dict as PARALLEL ordered key/value ValSeqs (same length; keys distinct).

    25	                 | #dictVal(Val, Entries, ValSeq, ValSeq)

    28	  rule <k> #dictAcc((Entry(K:Expr, V:Expr), REST:Entries), KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)

    30	  rule <k> KV:Val ~> #dictKey(V:Expr, REST:Entries, KS:ValSeq, VS:ValSeq)

     1	// reference/src/semantics/set.k — MPY-SET
     2	
     3	module MPY-SET
     4	  imports MPY-CORE
     5	
     6	  // a set value, carried as its distinct codes in first-seen order (order is irrelevant
     7	  // to membership/cardinality — the two observations sets support here).
     8	  syntax Val ::= setV(IntSeq)
     9	
    10	  // membership of a code in the accumulated distinct-code sequence
    11	  syntax Bool ::= codeIn(Int, IntSeq) [function, total]
    12	  rule codeIn(_:Int, .IntSeq)                => false
    13	  rule codeIn(C:Int, iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq)) => C ==Int H orBool codeIn(C, T)
    14	
    15	  // the distinct codes of CS (insert-if-absent fold, first-seen order)
    16	  syntax IntSeq ::= dedupCodes(IntSeq)         [function, total]
    17	                  | dedupFrom(IntSeq, IntSeq)  [function, total]
    18	  rule dedupCodes(CS:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(CS, .IntSeq)
    19	  rule dedupFrom(.IntSeq, ACC:IntSeq) => ACC
    20	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, ACC)
    21	       requires codeIn(C, ACC)
    22	  rule dedupFrom(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), ACC:IntSeq) => dedupFrom(S, snocCode(ACC, C))
    23	       requires notBool codeIn(C, ACC)
    24	
    25	  syntax IntSeq ::= snocCode(IntSeq, Int) [function, total]
    26	  rule snocCode(.IntSeq, C:Int)                => iCons(C, .IntSeq)
    27	  rule snocCode(iCons(H:Int, T:IntSeq), C:Int) => iCons(H, snocCode(T, C))
    28	
    29	  // ==== set equality: two sets are equal iff mutually subsuming ==============
    30	  // subsetCodes(A, B) — every code of A occurs in B (duplicates in A are harmless).
    31	  syntax Bool ::= subsetCodes(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    32	  rule subsetCodes(.IntSeq, _:IntSeq)                => true
    33	  rule subsetCodes(iCons(C:Int, S:IntSeq), B:IntSeq) => codeIn(C, B) andBool subsetCodes(S, B)
    34	
    35	  syntax Bool ::= sameSet(IntSeq, IntSeq) [function, total]
    36	  rule sameSet(A:IntSeq, B:IntSeq) => subsetCodes(A, B) andBool subsetCodes(B, A)
    37	
    38	  // set == set  (the only comparison sets support here)
    39	  rule applyCmp("==", setV(A:IntSeq), setV(B:IntSeq)) => sameSet(A, B)

     1	// reference/src/semantics/concrete.k — MPY-CONCRETE
     2	// Concrete-execution-only rules, visible ONLY to the llvm build (run.sh kompiles
     3	// MPY-CONCRETE; verification builds import MPY and never see these). Rationale:
     4	// a k-cell rule matching value constructors NARROWS abstract Vals in the haskell
     5	// backend ([concrete] is not respected on rewrite rules) — probed on
     6	// 26-remove-duplicates, where element compares branched into deepEqVS.

    11	  // deep equality for list compares whose elements are heap objects
    12	  // (list-of-lists): Python == is structural at every depth.

    14	       <heap> HP:Map </heap>
    15	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    16	  rule <k> Compare(list(A:ValSeq), CmpOp("!=", list(B:ValSeq))) => notBool deepEqVS(A, B, HP) ... </k>

    18	       requires hasRefVS(A) orBool hasRefVS(B)
    19	
    20	  // ==== keyed sort, concrete leg ============================================
    21	  // Computes each key by a REAL call through the uniform #callee machinery
    22	  // (closures, len, type objects all work), stable-inserts on the key, and
    23	  // allocates the result. priority(40) beats sort.k's opaque rules, so krun
    24	  // runs this and proofs (which never see MPY-CONCRETE) keep sortKeyVS.
    25	  syntax Val ::= kvP(Val, Val)
    26	  syntax KItem ::= #ksort(ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    27	                 | #ksIns(Val, ValSeq, Val, ValSeq, Bool)
    28	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), .Vals))
    29	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, false) ... </k>
    30	       [priority(40)]
    31	  rule <k> #applyK(toCall(builtinV("sorted")), (list(VS:ValSeq), kwV("key", KV:Val), kwV("reverse", RB:Bool), .Vals))
    32	        => #ksort(VS, KV, .ValSeq, RB) ... </k>
    33	       [priority(40)]
    34	  rule <k> #ksort(.ValSeq, _:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    35	        => #alloc(list(condRev(unpairVS(ACC), RB))) ... </k>
    36	  rule <k> #ksort(vCons(V:Val, R:ValSeq), KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    37	        => KV ~> #callee((V, .Exprs)) ~> #ksIns(V, R, KV, ACC, RB) ... </k>
    38	  rule <k> K:Val ~> #ksIns(V:Val, R:ValSeq, KV:Val, ACC:ValSeq, RB:Bool)
    39	        => #ksort(R, KV, insPair(ACC, K, V), RB) ... </k>
    40	       requires notBool isKwV(K)

+    return any(lo <= start <= hi for lo, hi in REACHABLE_RANGES.get(filename, []))
+
+
+def classify(document: dict[str, object]) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    path = str(document["path"])
+    filename = Path(path).name
+    kind = str(document["kind"])
+    start = int(document["start_line"])
+    text = str(document["text"])
+
+    if path == "/candidate/verification.k":
+        if kind == "rule" and start in {7, 24, 39, 45}:

+                "Expands a name to the submitted statement/body/closure/module term; "
+                "the independent pinning claim checks constructor identity.",
+            )
+        if kind == "rule" and start in {56, 59}:
+            return (
+                "CANDIDATE_TRUE_GUARDED_EQUATION",
+                "The pyMod==0 and pyMod=/=0 guards are disjoint and exhaustive; "
+                "the selected index is Python floor division on the used I>=0 domain.",
+            )
+        if kind == "rule" and start in {64, 65, 76, 77, 81}:
+            return (
+                "CANDIDATE_TRUE_STRUCTURAL_DEFINITION",
+                "Base/constructor equations are disjoint, structurally descending, "
+                "and define only the mathematical result summary.",
+            )

+            "Local declaration/import only; no operational <k> rewrite or simplification.",
+        )
+
+    if path == "/candidate/spec.k":
+        if kind == "claim":
+            return (

+                "Reachability claim, not an assumed equation; reconstructed by kprove.",
+            )

+

+
+

+
+

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Parse the complete legacy-selected-stage1 structured generation record."""

from __future__ import annotations

import collections
import json
from pathlib import Path


root = Path("/generation-evidence")
trace_files = sorted((root / "codex-trace").rglob("*"))
trace_files = [path for path in trace_files if path.is_file()]
assert len(trace_files) == 1

rows = [json.loads(line) for line in trace_files[0].read_text().splitlines()]
counts = collections.Counter(
    (row.get("type"), row.get("payload", {}).get("type")) for row in rows
)
invocation = json.loads((root / "invocation.json").read_text())
metrics = json.loads((root / "metrics.json").read_text())
usage = json.loads((root / "usage.json").read_text())
result = json.loads(Path("/generation-result.json").read_text())
task = json.loads(Path("/task.json").read_text())
run = json.loads(Path("/run.json").read_text())

session_meta = next(row for row in rows if row["type"] == "session_meta")
task_complete = next(
    row
    for row in rows
    if row["type"] == "event_msg"
    and row.get("payload", {}).get("type") == "task_complete"
)
selected = usage["selected_event"]
selected_row = rows[selected["line_number"] - 1]

assert session_meta["payload"]["session_id"] == invocation["session_id"]
assert invocation["session_id"] == result["session_id"]
assert task_complete["payload"]["last_agent_message"] == (
    root / "codex-last.txt"
).read_text()
assert selected_row["type"] == "event_msg"
assert selected_row["payload"]["type"] == "token_count"
assert invocation["status"] == metrics["status"] == result["status"] == "SUCCEEDED"
assert invocation["result_marker"] == result["result_marker"] == "KPROVE_PASSED"
assert task["problem_id"] == "33-sort-third"
assert task["condition"] == run["condition"]

output = (root / "codex-output.log").read_text(errors="strict")
assert "kprove spec.k --definition verification-kompiled --spec-module SPEC" in output
assert "RESULT: KPROVE_PASSED" in output

print(f"trace_file={trace_files[0]}")
print(f"trace_lines={len(rows)}")
for key, value in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda item: str(item[0])):
    print(f"trace_count[{key}]={value}")
print(f"session_id={invocation['session_id']}")
print(f"invocation_exit_code={invocation['exit_code']}")
print(f"duration_s={metrics['duration_s']}")
print(f"usage_status={usage['status']}")
print(f"selected_usage_event={selected}")
print(f"generation_result={result['status']} marker={result['result_marker']}")
print("generation records parsed completely; claims remain untrusted")

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /audit-output/REVIEW.md
+# Independent adversarial review: 33-sort-third
+
+The candidate contains a legitimate, non-vacuous partial-correctness proof of
+the submitted program under the supplied semantics. The proof executes the
+translated body, its generalized loop claim closes, the full entry proof closes
+from a clean rebuild, and mutations of both the executed body and final result
+are rejected. I assign `CONCERNS / LEGIT`, rather than `PASS`, because the
+supplied semantics intentionally leaves the value-level meaning of symbolic
+`sorted` and opaque sorted-list access outside K: the theorem is conditional on
+the documented `sortVS`/`valSeqAt` contract, supported by ground execution and
+finite differential tests but not a universal K connection theorem.
+
+The complete command ledger is
+[`evidence/COMMANDS.md`](evidence/COMMANDS.md). All executable work used source
+copies in `/tmp/audit-work/33-sort-third`; no candidate definition or cache was
+reused.
+
+## 1. Input and provenance integrity
+
+`/audit-input.json` declares:
+
+- problem `33-sort-third`, condition `semantics`;
+- `semantics_mode: SUPPLIED_SEMANTICS`;
+- record layout `legacy-selected-stage1`; and
+- complete input provenance.
+
+The trusted `/reference/reference-semantics` mount is present, as required for
+this mode. There is no rendered-mode contradiction.
+
+I read every record required for this layout: `/run.json`, `/task.json`,
+`/generation-result.json`, `invocation.json`, `metrics.json`, `usage.json`,
+`codex-last.txt`, `codex-output.log`, `prompt.txt`, and the complete 238-line
+JSONL trace. I also inspected the present legacy records
+`legacy-metrics.json` and `legacy-run-input.json`. Historical
+`runtime-metrics.json` is absent, but it is not required for this legacy layout.
+The generation record claims `KPROVE_PASSED`; that claim was not used as proof
+evidence.
+
+The independently parsed trace has one start and one completion event, 38 tool
+calls and 38 results, ten patch calls and results, and a session ID matching
+the invocation/result records. See
+[`generation-record-summary.log`](evidence/generation-record-summary.log) and
+its reviewer script.
+
+Integrity checks passed:
+
+- The campaign-lock object is exactly equal to the `audit_campaign` block.
+  The lock SHA-256 is
+  `ad5dfcc006af70c4d0d2c6641f0878a6c54a266e9ad2b54cd225b2381a78d745`,
+  and `/audit-prompt.md` matches the lock's
+  `999526823ad89bcd9b6e77db8f5f1189f629c86c9ecb308094b84c7161c04e5a`.
+- Every recorded regular-file digest checked by
+  [`integrity_check.py`](evidence/integrity_check.py) matches, including the
+  trusted canonical, prompt, translator, run/task/result records, invocation,
+  metrics, usage, prompt, output, and last-message files.
+- The candidate prompt and translator are byte-identical to the trusted
+  mounts.
+- Candidate and trusted semantics have the same 25-entry recursive shape and
+  byte-identical files. Every entry is a real directory or regular file; there
+  are no links, additions, omissions, or mistyped entries.
+- Independent legacy pipeline tree hashes are
+  `3fc5c84a...` for the candidate (matching the stage-1 workspace record),
+  `61020c40...` for the trace (matching `usage.json`), and `4e06397a...` for

+  read-only.

+Evidence: [`integrity.log`](evidence/integrity.log),
+[`mount-candidate.log`](evidence/mount-candidate.log), and the two companion
+mount logs.
+
+No audit-infrastructure breach was found.
+
+## 2. Program fidelity and canonical comparison
+
+The source contract says that `sort_third(l)` returns a list whose positions
+not divisible by three equal the original positions, while the values at
+indices divisible by three are those original every-third values in sorted
+order. The trusted canonical copies the input, sorts `l[::3]`, assigns that
+slice back, and returns the copy.
+
+The submitted implementation computes `thirds = sorted(l[::3])`, traverses the
+original list once with index `i`, appends `thirds[i // 3]` when
+`i % 3 == 0`, and otherwise appends the original element. This is the same
+transformation for finite plain lists whose selected elements can be sorted.
+It also returns a fresh list and does not mutate the input.
+
+Trusted regeneration was exact:
+
+```text
+python3 /reference/py2mpy.py solution.py > regenerated-solution.mpy
+cmp --verbose regenerated-solution.mpy solution.mpy
+```
+
+Both commands exited 0. Both MPY files hash to
+`a6f1d547a4bfc1dacc8f0808923b8277fc42e24ce17924fd8091c4b59469e58a`.
+See [`translation-hashes.log`](evidence/translation-hashes.log).
+
+The independent differential test imports `/reference/canonical.py` and the

+homogeneous strings and floats, all lists of lengths 0 through 7 over

+All 8,290 cases agreed, with no input mutation:
+
+```text
+cases=8290 mismatches=0 input_mutations=0
+```
+
+The exact generated inputs are
+[`differential_inputs.jsonl`](evidence/differential_inputs.jsonl), SHA-256
+`8350e442...`; the oracle/test is
+[`differential_test.py`](evidence/differential_test.py).
+
+## 3. Clean proof reconstruction
+
+Only `solution.py`, `solution.mpy`, `verification.k`, `spec.k`, the trusted
+translator/prompt, and a fresh copy of the trusted semantics were placed in
+scratch. Candidate `__pycache__`, compiled definitions, and any generated
+caches were excluded.

+The observed `kompile` and `kprove` version is K `v7.1.293`, matching the
+campaign lock.
+
+### Concrete definition
+
+I compiled `MPY-KRUN` with the LLVM backend from the scratch source tree. The
+build exited 0. A reviewer-authored translated K test module exercised empty,
+one-, two-, three-, and four-element boundary lists, the second prompt example,
+and a ten-element negative-value case. `krun` exited 0, ended with `.K`,

+[`kompile-concrete.log`](evidence/kompile-concrete.log),
+[`krun-concrete.log`](evidence/krun-concrete.log), and
+[`audit_concrete_tests.py`](evidence/audit_concrete_tests.py).

+The concrete compiler warned that several supplied `[total]` functions are
+non-exhaustive over the complete `Val` universe. Only `valSeqAt` is on this
+program's symbolic path; its deliberate opaque-total role is accounted for in
+Stages 5 and 7.
+
+### Proof definition and claims
+
+The Haskell proof definition compiled from source with exit 0. The generalized
+loop claim alone returned `#Top`, exit 0. The submitted unfiltered positive
+command, which supplies that loop theorem while proving the entry claim, also
+returned `#Top`, exit 0:
+
+```text
+kprove spec.k --definition audit-verification-kompiled --spec-module SPEC
+#Top
+```
+
+Evidence: [`kompile-proof.log`](evidence/kompile-proof.log),
+[`kprove-loop.log`](evidence/kprove-loop.log), and
+[`kprove-all.log`](evidence/kprove-all.log).
+
+For diagnostic clarity, filtering the helper out and asking for only
+`SPEC.sort-third-correct` exits 1 at the real `#iterNext/#loopStep` state. This
+does not contradict the positive command: the entry theorem intentionally uses
+the separately proved loop circularity, and the unfiltered command proves both.
+The residual is preserved in
+[`kprove-correct.log`](evidence/kprove-correct.log).
+
+## 4. Adequacy and real-program pinning
+
+### Plain-language claims
+
+`sort-third-loop` assumes:
+
+- the active computation is exactly
+  `#loop(list(INPUT), Name("value"), sortThirdBody) ~> CONT`;
+- the current frame binds a nonnegative integer `i = I`, an arbitrary retained
+  `l`, prior loop value `OLD`, result reference `HR`, and sorted-list reference
+  `HT`;
+- `HT` holds `SORTED` and `HR` holds already-built prefix `ACC`; and
+- omitted scope/heap/configuration portions are framed.
+
+It concludes that the loop is consumed and `CONT` resumes; `i` increases by
+`vsLen(INPUT)`, `value` becomes the last iterated element (or stays `OLD` for
+empty input), and the result heap becomes
+`sortThirdAcc(INPUT, SORTED, I, ACC)`. All other framed state is preserved.
+
+`sort-third-correct` starts from a clean module configuration and executes:

explicit `symbol(...)` declarations, and 22 `no-evaluators` declarations.
There are no local `[simplification]` or `[functional]` declarations.

### Construct coverage and execution

| Submitted construct | Declaration/rules | Audited effect |
|---|---|---|
| module/function definition | `syntax.k`; `core.k:124-127`; `functions.k:14-16` | loads the real binding and closure |
| call/arguments | `call.k:16-32,38-50,69-75`; `core.k:183-191` | callee then left-to-right arguments, fresh frame, exact continuation |
| names/scopes | `core.k:130-181` | local lookup then builtins; `sorted` binding is pinned |
| list literal/allocation | `list.k:13-20`; `core.k:117-121` | fresh `result` at location 2 |
| slice `l[::3]` | `subscript.k:43-114` | bounds normalize to start 0, stop length, step 3; allocates location 0 |
| `sorted(...)` | `sort.k:18-37`; `call.k` dereference | dereferences slice, allocates location 1 containing `sortVS` |
| `for`/target binding | `controls.k:62-74`; `list.k:9-10`; `tuple.k:31-41` | structural list iteration and current-frame binding |
| `%`, `//`, `+`, `==` | `operators.k`; `int.k:9-27` | Python floored modulo/division for divisor 3 and integer branch test |
| `if` | `controls.k:50-54` | truthy Boolean branch, disjoint cases |
| subscripting `thirds` | `subscript.k:25-41` | heap dereference and nonnegative positional access |
| `result.append` | `call.k`; `list.k:52-55` | priority rule preserves receiver reference and updates heap in place |
| `i += 1` | `controls.k:20-23`; `int.k:9` | current-frame integer update |
| return/pop | `functions.k:77-90` | returns `ref(2)`, restores caller, preserves escaping heap |

Allocation and control footprints match the final claim: the slice, sorted
copy, and result consume locations 0, 1, and 2; appends allocate nothing;
callee scope 1 is removed; the return reference and all three lists remain.
The relevant priority rules preempt only their corresponding generic paths:
list slicing beats generic slicing, append beats pure method fallback, and heap
dereference beats generic value dispatch. Guards are disjoint on the actual
plain-frame/int/list path.

### Candidate-local extensions

The four constructor aliases (`sortThirdBody`, `sortThirdFunctionBody`,
`sortThirdClosure`, `sortThirdModule`) exactly name submitted syntax and do not
match or replace an operational `<k>` region. `thirdValue` has disjoint and
exhaustive `pyMod == 0` / `=/= 0` guards. `sortThirdAcc` and
`lastLoopValue` have disjoint empty/constructor equations and structurally
descend. `sortThird` is a one-equation definitional summary. All eight declared
functions are covered on their used domains; the 11 equations have no
conflicting overlap. There is no candidate priority rule, simplification,
opaque symbol, oracle, or execution-bypassing operational bridge.

The loop claim is a derived circularity, not a rewrite axiom asserted without
proof. Its arbitrary `CONT` is sound because the exact loop body contains no
return, break, exception, allocation, or cleanup effect; the fixed semantics
iterates to completion and resumes that continuation. The body mutation
demonstrates that it is sensitive to the displaced computation.

### Supplied boundary and unused rules

The only result-bearing opaque symbol on this proof path is the supplied
`sortVS`. `sort.k` routes the real `sorted` builtin to a fresh list containing
that symbol and provides ground Int/str insertion-sort equations. Symbolically,
`sortVS` is intentionally total and opaque. `valSeqAt` has correct constructor
equations for nonnegative in-bounds access and is deliberately `[total]` on an
opaque sequence. Thus the proof is parametric in these fixed language
primitives; it does not invent their values.

The other explicit opaque symbols are the supplied float primitives
`intFloatDiv`, `divII`, `floatMod`, `floatLt`, `absF`, `floorFI`, `toF`,
`ceilF`, `subF`, `divF`, `addF`, `mulF`, `powF`, `gtF`, `eqF`,
`decStrToF`, `divFloatIntV`, `intToF`, `truncF`, `roundF`, `roundFN`,
`sqrtF`, plus `sortKeyVS` and `md5hexCodes`. None occurs in either claim or a
reachable target state.

The inventory classifies 715 fixed-semantics sentences as unreachable from the
submitted constructor term (other AST constructs, types, methods, builtins, or
concrete-only alternatives). I checked their heads and priority/owise overlaps
against the reachable terms; none can fire on or alter this proof. This review
does not claim that the intentionally minimal supplied language is a complete
Python semantics for those unused constructs.

I found no candidate or reachable fixed rule that enables a false conclusion
on the intended list-of-sortable-values domain. Accordingly, there is no
unsoundness allegation requiring a false-conclusion witness. The opaque-sort
issue is instead an explicit trust/evidence boundary.

## 6. Fresh non-vacuity test

The candidate supplied no `spec-vacuity.k`; I created an independent mutation.
It leaves the execution and loop theorem unchanged but changes the final
result-bearing heap obligation from:

```text
2 |-> list(sortThird(INPUT))
```

to:

```text
2 |-> list(vCons(999, sortThird(INPUT)))
```

The mutated spec parses/builds and reaches the real final configuration. Proof
then exits 1 with `WarnStuckClaimState` on the unmet equality:

```text
sortThirdAcc(...) = vCons(999, sortThirdAcc(...))
```

This is the expected result obligation, not a parser error, timeout, or
unrelated crash. The satisfying ground witness `INPUT=[]` yields `[]` from
both Python implementations while the mutation requires `[999]`.

Evidence: [`spec-vacuity.k`](evidence/spec-vacuity.k),
[`kprove-vacuity.log`](evidence/kprove-vacuity.log),
[`vacuity_witness.py`](evidence/vacuity_witness.py), and
[`vacuity-witness.log`](evidence/vacuity-witness.log).

Non-vacuity gate: PASS.

## 7. Proven versus assumed accounting

### Formally established

Under the imported supplied K theory, for every finite `INPUT:ValSeq`, normal
execution of the exact submitted translated module from the claim's clean
configuration returns reference 2. Its list is:

```text
sortThirdAcc(
  INPUT,
  sortVS(buildVS(INPUT, 0, vsLen(INPUT), 3)),
  0,
  .ValSeq)
```

The fold preserves every non-multiple-of-three input value at its position and,
at every multiple of three, inserts the corresponding indexed value from the
supplied sorted every-third sequence. The proof also establishes the claimed
scope, heap, allocation, stack, return, exception, and exit-code post-state.
It is unrestricted in list length; it is not finite unrolling.

### Trust ledger

| Boundary | Influence | Status/evidence |
|---|---|---|
| K 7.1.293 frontend and Haskell reachability backend | parsing, compilation, symbolic execution, circularity soundness | toolchain/campaign assumption; fresh successful rebuild and mutation discrimination |
| Trusted `py2mpy.py` | Python-to-constructor identity | mounted hash, byte-identical regeneration |
| Supplied operational semantics | evaluation order, scopes, allocation, calls, loops, return | exact candidate/trusted semantics identity; exhaustive source inventory; concrete K executions |
| `sortVS` contract: ascending permutation of its input | all returned values at divisible-by-three indices and human “sorted” intent | fixed external builtin boundary, not candidate code; ground Int/str equations, K examples, and Python differential evidence; no symbolic universal K theorem |
| `valSeqAt` totality on opaque sorted sequences, with actual accesses in bounds | selected returned elements | fixed supplied boundary; constructor equations plus informal length/index argument; depends on `sortVS` preserving length |
| Canonical-to-rewrite equivalence | connection to original HumanEval implementation | algorithmic inspection and 8,290 finite differential cases; not a universal machine proof |

The same `sortVS`/`valSeqAt` terms appear in execution and the postcondition,
but this is not a candidate-created circular oracle: they are fixed external
language primitives deliberately outside the program-defined code being
proved. The theorem is interpretation-parametric/conditional on that named
contract. The limitation is that the supplied source contains comments and
ground implementations, not a bridge-free symbolic theorem proving ordering,
permutation, and length preservation for arbitrary `ValSeq`.

The proof does not establish full CPython behavior for heterogeneous
incomparable objects, user-defined comparison side effects, exceptions,
arbitrary object identity/aliasing, or unsupported Python constructs. Those are
outside this finite plain-list HumanEval execution model. Differential tests
support, but do not universally prove, the Python/K and summary/intent bridges.

Kit validation gates:

- Gate A, real-program soundness: PASS.
- Gate B, intent adequacy: PASS for the material HumanEval list domain,
  conditional on the supplied `sorted` primitive.
- Gate C, trust/evidence auditability: PASS with a disclosed finite-evidence
  limitation.

The proof is therefore legitimate and result-constraining, with a non-fatal
trust-boundary concern under the benchmark's decision mapping.
